sources.entry: Brood Box by stacklok - CLI tool for running coding agents inside hardware-isolated microVMs

summary.one_liner: Brood Box (bbox) is an experimental CLI that runs coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode inside hardware-isolated libkrun/KVM microVMs, with a copy-on-write workspace snapshot that you review file by file before changes are flushed back.
keywords: run ai coding assistant in vm
summary.what_it_does: Brood Box launches a coding agent in a lightweight VM rather than a container, so the agent does not share the host kernel. By default it creates a copy-on-write snapshot of the current workspace, boots a microVM from the agent's OCI image, and opens an interactive SSH session in the guest. When the agent exits, the VM is stopped and a SHA-256 based differ shows unified diffs per file so you can accept or reject each change, and accepted changes are flushed back with hash re-verification. It forwards only the environment variables and git credentials you configure, and can restrict outbound traffic with egress profiles (permissive, standard, locked) plus extra allowed hostnames. It can also proxy ToolHive MCP servers into the VM, and a run-image subcommand runs an arbitrary OCI image as an ephemeral one-shot. A direct workspace mode skips snapshot isolation for trusted, turn-by-turn work.
use_cases: run claude code without giving it full access to my machine
review every file change an ai agent makes before it lands
sandbox a coding agent in a microvm
restrict network access for an llm coding agent
run an arbitrary container image as a throwaway agent sandbox
keep API keys away from an autonomous coding tool
how_to_run: Install a release binary (tar xzf bbox-linux-amd64.tar.gz; sudo mv bbox /usr/local/bin/) or build with: task build
stack: SSH (embedded server in bbox-init guest init)
notable: Custom Go init binary (bbox-init) runs as PID 1 in the guest, with no shell scripts or external sshd
Interactive per-file diff review of the agent's changes, with the VM stopped before review
Three egress profiles (permissive, standard, locked) with DNS-hostname allow-listing
Security-sensitive files such as .env, *.pem, .ssh/ and .aws/ are always excluded from snapshots
run-image subcommand runs any OCI image as an ephemeral sandbox with safer defaults
caveats: Explicitly EXPERIMENTAL: APIs, CLI flags and config format may change without notice
Requires Linux with /dev/kvm accessible, or macOS with Hypervisor.framework on Apple Silicon
direct workspace mode writes straight to your files with no review or undo, and it requires --yes on first use
Building from source requires Go 1.26+ and Task; agent images are pulled from ghcr.io
